title: Replacing HTTP/REST with Custom Sockets to Save Bandwidth
pattern: Writing a custom TCP socket protocol and binary parser to replace simple HTTP or gRPC APIs to "save protocol overhead."
why_bad: Custom protocols take months to design, are highly prone to security bugs, and cannot utilize standard proxies, load balancers, or caching servers. The bandwidth savings for typical low-traffic APIs are completely negligible [211, 495].
detection: A custom socket layer, manually parsing raw byte streams (`TcpStream`) for application queries when HTTP, gRPC, or standard frameworks are applicable.
counterexample: Extremely high-frequency real-time gaming protocols or low-latency telemetry data. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Use standard HTTP or gRPC frameworks with standard serialization formats.
source: *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, Chapter 10 (p. 211); *Systems Performance*, Chapter 10, Section 10.5 (p. 495).
